object_types.name: Patient
object_types.definition: A person who books and attends appointments at the clinic.

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments. Every appointment is booked by exactly one patient, and a patient can have many appointments... Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: PatientId
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a patient, issued on their clinic card.

source_references.excerpt: Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: Doctor
object_types.definition: A medical professional who examines patients and conducts appointments at the clinic.

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor. Doctors see many patients across their appointments... Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: LicenseNumber
object_types.definition: The unique professional license number that identifies a doctor.

source_references.excerpt: Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: Appointment
object_types.definition: A scheduled time slot during which a patient meets with a doctor at the clinic.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is booked by exactly one patient... Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: AppointmentNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier assigned to an appointment upon creation.

source_references.excerpt: Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: ExamRoom
object_types.definition: A physical room in the clinic where appointments can be conducted.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: RoomNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for an exam room.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: Specialty
object_types.definition: A medical field or practice area in which a doctor specializes, such as cardiology or general practice.

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.

object_types.name: AppointmentDate
object_types.definition: The calendar date on which an appointment is scheduled.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

object_types.name: TimeSlot
object_types.definition: A fixed time period during the day at which appointments can be booked, such as 09:00 or 09:30.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

object_types.name: AppointmentStatus
object_types.definition: The current state of an appointment in its lifecycle.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled... An appointment always has exactly one status from that list.

object_types.name: VisitReason
object_types.definition: The reason or chief complaint provided by the patient when booking an appointment.

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking.

object_types.name: FollowUpNote
object_types.definition: A clinical note or follow-up instruction attached to an appointment by the doctor after the visit.

source_references.excerpt: After the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note. At most one follow-up note per appointment.

ambiguities.description: Exam room association with appointments: The transcript mentions exam rooms and their room numbers, but does not explicitly state whether appointments are assigned to exam rooms. It is unclear if an 'Appointment is held in ExamRoom' relationship should be modeled. Should this be captured as a separate fact type with uniqueness constraints?

Facilitator: Let's go through how appointments work at the clinic.

ambiguities.description: Follow-up note optionality: The transcript states 'the doctor can attach a follow-up note' and 'At most one follow-up note per appointment', clearly indicating optionality (0..1 multiplicity on the appointment side). However, it does not clarify the reverse: if a follow-up note is created, must it be attached to an appointment, or can orphaned notes exist?

source_references.excerpt: After the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note. At most one follow-up note per appointment.

ambiguities.description: Visit reason optionality: The transcript states 'An appointment can have a visit reason', indicating the reason is optional (0..1). However, it does not clarify whether a visit reason value, once recorded, can be reused across multiple appointments, or whether it must be unique to that appointment.

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking.

ambiguities.description: Appointment date and time slot as independent values: The model treats AppointmentDate and TimeSlot as separate value types. It is unclear whether the clinic uses absolute timestamps or whether date+time are always managed separately. Should TimeSlot be a structured entity (e.g., with start and end times) or remain a simple text value like '09:00'?

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

ambiguities.description: Doctor specialty as a simple value vs. a reference: Specialty is currently modeled as a value type (text), but it could alternatively be modeled as an entity type if specialties have their own identifiers or properties (e.g., specialty_code, description). The transcript does not clarify whether specialty is just a descriptive string or a reference to a managed specialty master list.
